nutrition.intro: Nutrition supports your training and daily energy. These goals focus on sustainable habits rather than restrictive diets.

goals.title: Balanced Daily Intake
goals.description: Aim for a plate that includes lean protein, whole grains, healthy fats, and plenty of vegetables at most meals.
tips: Fill half your plate with vegetables
Choose whole grains over refined carbs
Stay hydrated — roughly 8 cups of water daily

goals.title: Muscle Building Support
goals.description: Adequate protein and calories help repair and grow muscle tissue after resistance training.
tips: Target 1.6–2.2 g protein per kg body weight
Don't fear carbohydrates — they fuel training

goals.title: Weight Management
goals.description: Sustainable weight change comes from consistent calorie balance combined with regular activity.
tips: Focus on whole, minimally processed foods
Track portions without obsessing over numbers
Avoid extreme restriction — it rarely lasts

lifestyle.intro: Fitness looks different depending on your background, schedule, and responsibilities. Find guidance that fits your life.

profiles.title: Busy Professionals
profiles.description: Limited time doesn't mean limited results. Short, efficient workouts and meal prep strategies work best.
recommendations: Batch-cook proteins and grains on weekends
Walk during phone calls or meetings
Set a consistent bedtime for recovery

profiles.title: Students
profiles.description: Budget-friendly nutrition and flexible training that fits around classes and study sessions.
recommendations: Use campus gym or bodyweight workouts
Buy frozen vegetables and bulk grains
Limit late-night snacking with planned meals

profiles.title: Parents & Caregivers
profiles.description: Integrate family activity and realistic meal planning when time and energy are scarce.
recommendations: Family walks or bike rides after dinner
Simple one-pot meals with balanced macros
Exercise during naptime or early mornings
Involve kids in meal prep when possible

profiles.title: Older Adults (55+)
profiles.description: Focus on strength, balance, and bone health with safe, progressive programming.
recommendations: Balance exercises daily (single-leg stands, tai chi)
Adequate protein to prevent muscle loss
Consult your doctor before new programs

healthInfo.intro: Quick, evidence-informed summaries of topics that matter for your health and fitness journey.

summaries.title: How Much Exercise Do Adults Need?
summaries.summary: The WHO recommends at least 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity or 75 minutes of vigorous activity per week, plus muscle-strengthening activities on 2 or more days.
summaries.source: World Health Organization — Physical Activity Guidelines

summaries.title: Protein & Muscle Protein Synthesis
summaries.summary: Consuming 20–40g of high-quality protein per meal maximally stimulates muscle repair. Spreading intake across the day is more effective than one large dose.

summaries.title: The Role of Fiber
summaries.summary: Dietary fiber supports gut health, helps manage blood sugar, and is associated with lower cardiovascular disease risk. Aim for 25–38g daily from whole food sources.

summaries.title: Resistance Training & Bone Health
summaries.summary: Weight-bearing and resistance exercises stimulate bone formation and help prevent osteoporosis, especially important for women over 50 and older adults.

blog.intro: Articles, practical tips, and updates from the FitWell Education team.

posts.title: Starting Strong: Your First Week of Training
posts.excerpt: New to exercise? Here's how to build a habit that sticks without burning out.
posts.content: The first week is about showing up, not perfection. Choose two or three days for short workouts, focus on form over intensity, and celebrate consistency. Rest days are part of the plan — your body needs time to adapt.

posts.title: Meal Prep Without the Overwhelm
posts.excerpt: Simple strategies to eat well during a busy week without spending your entire Sunday in the kitchen.
posts.content: Start with one protein, one grain, and one vegetable batch-cooked on the weekend. Mix and match through the week. Keep healthy snacks visible — cut fruit, nuts, yogurt — so convenience foods aren't your only option.

posts.title: Why Rest Days Matter
posts.excerpt: Recovery isn't lazy — it's when your body actually gets stronger.
posts.content: Muscle repair, hormone balance, and nervous system recovery all happen during rest. Active recovery like walking or stretching can help, but avoid stacking intense sessions back-to-back without adequate sleep and nutrition.
